title: How to Make a Dish Less Spicy
paragraphs: Many people like adding spice to their food, but too much could leave your mouth feeling like it's on fire.
Instead of throwing away a dish you've made that's just too spicy, here are some things that may help.

The spiciness in hot peppers comes from a chemical called capsaicin, which is an alkaline oil. Since acids are the chemical opposite of alkalis, they can be used to neutralize the taste — so if you want your dish to be less spicy, add something acidic to it, like lemon or vinegar.
Capsaicin also dissolves in fat, so you can add fat to your dish to reduce the spiciness. For example, you can use milk, yogurt or butter if they work well with your dish.
You might also add coconut milk or peanut butter, which taste great in some Asian dishes, like curries or pad thai.

Sweet things don't only taste good with spicy ones, they can also neutralize them. You could add a little bit of honey or sugar, but be careful not to add too much — this can change the taste of your dish, and might make it more like a dessert!

While it won't make the dish itself less spicy, serving your food with something starchy could help reduce the impact of the spice. Based on what's in your dish, you might serve it with rice, pasta, bread or potatoes, for example.
